name: Carrie Brown
summary: Carrie Brown, known on the Bowery as "Old Shakespeare," was found strangled and mutilated in Room 31 of the East River Hotel in Manhattan on April 24, 1891.

name: Andrew & Abby Borden
summary: Andrew Borden and his wife Abby were found hacked to death in their Fall River, Massachusetts home. Their daughter Lizzie was acquitted of the murders.

name: Stanford White
summary: Architect Stanford White, 52, was shot dead on June 25, 1906, at the rooftop theater of Madison Square Garden by Harry K. Thaw, husband of Evelyn Nesbit.

name: Virginia Christian Case
summary: Ida Belote, 51, was killed in her Hampton, Virginia, home on March 18, 1912. Her 16-year-old laundress, Virginia Christian, was convicted of first-degree murder by an all-white, all-male jury in April 1912 and was electrocuted…

name: New Orleans Axeman Victims
summary: An unidentified attacker known as the Axeman struck homes in and around New Orleans between May 1918 and October 1919, killing six people and injuring several others, many of them Italian grocers and their families.

name: Virginia Rappe
summary: Actress Virginia Rappe died in San Francisco on September 9, 1921, of peritonitis from a ruptured bladder, four days after falling ill at a Labor Day party in Roscoe "Fatty" Arbuckle's suite at the St. Francis Hotel.

name: William Desmond Taylor
summary: Film director William Desmond Taylor, 49, was shot in the back at his bungalow in the Alvarado Court Apartments in Los Angeles on the evening of February 1, 1922; his body was found the next morning.

name: Bobby Franks
summary: Fourteen-year-old Bobby Franks was abducted and killed in Chicago on May 21, 1924, by Nathan Leopold and Richard Loeb, two wealthy students.

name: Judge Joseph Force Crater
summary: New York Supreme Court Justice Joseph Force Crater, 41, vanished on the evening of August 6, 1930, after dining with two companions at a restaurant on West 45th Street in Manhattan.

name: Starr Faithfull
summary: Starr Faithfull, 25, was found dead on the beach at Long Beach, New York, on June 8, 1931, three days after leaving her family's Manhattan apartment. An autopsy found she had drowned and had bruises and a sedative in her system.

name: Charles Lindbergh Jr.
summary: The infant son of aviator Charles Lindbergh was kidnapped from the family estate in Hopewell, New Jersey. A ransom was paid but the baby's body was found two months later.

name: Paul Bern
summary: MGM producer Paul Bern, 42, was found dead of a gunshot wound at his Beverly Hills home on September 5, 1932, two months after marrying actress Jean Harlow. A note was found and a coroner's jury ruled the death a suicide.

name: Cleveland Torso Murders
summary: At least 12 people were killed, decapitated and dismembered in and around Cleveland's Kingsbury Run between September 1935 and August 1938. Only two victims were positively identified and no one was ever convicted.

name: Thelma Todd
summary: Film actress Thelma Todd, 29, was found dead of carbon monoxide poisoning in her car inside a Pacific Palisades garage on December 16, 1935.

name: Amelia Earhart
summary: Pioneer aviator Amelia Earhart and navigator Fred Noonan vanished over the Pacific Ocean during her attempt to circumnavigate the globe. She was declared legally dead in 1939.

name: Betty June Binnicker & Mary Emma Thames
summary: Betty June Binnicker, 11, and Mary Emma Thames, 8, were found killed in Alcolu, South Carolina, on March 23, 1944. George Stinney Jr., a 14-year-old Black boy, was convicted in a one-day trial and executed on June 16, 1944.

name: Recy Taylor
summary: Recy Taylor, a 24-year-old Black sharecropper, was abducted and raped by six white men while walking home from church in Abbeville, Alabama, on September 3, 1944. Two all-white grand juries declined to indict anyone.

name: Suzanne Degnan
summary: Six-year-old Suzanne Degnan was abducted from her bedroom in Chicago's Edgewater neighborhood on January 7, 1946, and killed. William Heirens, 17, pleaded guilty in September 1946 to her murder and two others and received three…

name: Texarkana Moonlight Murders
summary: Five people were killed and three wounded in four nighttime attacks in and around Texarkana, on the Texas-Arkansas border, between February 22 and May 3, 1946. The attacker, called the Phantom Killer, was never identified.

name: Elizabeth Short (The Black Dahlia)
summary: The mutilated body of 22-year-old Elizabeth Short was found in a vacant lot in Los Angeles. Her body had been severed at the waist, drained of blood, and posed.

name: Beverly Potts
summary: Ten-year-old Beverly Potts disappeared on the evening of August 24, 1951, after attending a Showagon performance at Halloran Park, a short walk from her home on Cleveland's west side.

name: Bobby Greenlease
summary: Six-year-old Bobby Greenlease was taken from his Kansas City school on September 28, 1953, by Bonnie Heady and killed the same day by Carl Austin Hall. His family paid a $600,000 ransom before his body was found.

name: Frank Olson
summary: Army biochemist Frank Olson, 43, died on November 28, 1953, after falling from a window of the Hotel Statler in New York, nine days after CIA colleagues gave him LSD without his knowledge. The death was treated as a suicide.

name: Janett Christman
summary: Thirteen-year-old Janett Christman was sexually assaulted and strangled on the night of March 18, 1950, while babysitting at a home in Columbia, Missouri.

name: Marilyn Sheppard
summary: Marilyn Sheppard was bludgeoned to death in her Bay Village, Ohio home. Her husband, Dr. Sam Sheppard, was convicted of murder in 1954 but his conviction was overturned. Retried in 1966, he was acquitted.

name: Emmett Till
summary: Fourteen-year-old Emmett Till, a Black teenager from Chicago, was abducted and brutally murdered near Money, Mississippi, on August 28, 1955, after allegedly whistling at a white woman. Roy Bryant and J.W.

name: Barbara & Patricia Grimes
summary: Sisters Barbara, 15, and Patricia Grimes, 12, vanished on December 28, 1956, after going to see an Elvis Presley film at Chicago's Brighton Theater.

name: Daniel Barter
summary: Four-year-old Daniel "Danny" Barter vanished on June 18, 1959, from his family's campsite on Perdido Bay, Alabama. A search lasting more than a week, with hundreds of volunteers, divers and bloodhounds, found no trace of him.

name: Henry Lee Lucas Victims
summary: Henry Lee Lucas confessed to hundreds of murders but most were unverifiable. He was confirmed in several cases including the murder of his mother and with accomplice Ottis Toole.

name: Boston Strangler Victims
summary: Thirteen women were strangled in the Boston area between 1962 and 1964. Albert DeSalvo confessed to all 13 murders but was never tried for them. DNA evidence collected in 2013 linked DeSalvo to the last victim, Mary Sullivan.

name: William 'Billy' Jones Jr.
summary: Three-year-old William "Billy" Jones Jr. disappeared on December 17, 1962, while playing outside with his younger sister in Vineland, New Jersey. He was last seen near a neighbor's house at about 11:45 a.m.

name: 16th Street Baptist Church Bombing Victims
summary: A dynamite bomb planted by Ku Klux Klan members killed Addie Mae Collins, Carole Robertson and Cynthia Wesley, all 14, and Denise McNair, 11, at Birmingham's 16th Street Baptist Church on September 15, 1963.

name: Frank Sinatra Jr. Kidnapping
summary: Singer Frank Sinatra Jr., 19, was abducted at gunpoint from Harrah's Club Lodge at Lake Tahoe on December 8, 1963. His father paid a $240,000 ransom and he was freed unharmed in Los Angeles on December 11.

name: John F. Kennedy Assassination
summary: President John F. Kennedy, 46, was shot dead in his motorcade in Dealey Plaza, Dallas, on November 22, 1963. Lee Harvey Oswald was charged but was killed by Jack Ruby two days later and never tried.

name: Medgar Evers
summary: Medgar Evers, 37, the NAACP's first field secretary in Mississippi, was shot in the back outside his Jackson home shortly after midnight on June 12, 1963, and died within the hour.

name: James Chaney, Andrew Goodman & Michael Schwerner
summary: Civil rights workers James Chaney, 21, Andrew Goodman, 20, and Michael Schwerner, 24, were killed by Ku Klux Klan members in Neshoba County, Mississippi, on June 21, 1964. Their bodies were found 44 days later.

name: Kitty Genovese
summary: Kitty Genovese, 28, was stabbed to death near her apartment in Kew Gardens, Queens, early on March 13, 1964. Winston Moseley confessed, was convicted of murder that June and died in prison in 2016.

name: Alice Crimmins
summary: Eddie Crimmins Jr., 5, and his sister Alice Marie "Missy" Crimmins, 4, were reported missing from their Queens apartment on July 14, 1965, and were found dead five days apart.

name: Jimmie Lee Jackson
summary: Jimmie Lee Jackson, 26, a church deacon and voting rights activist, was shot by Alabama state trooper James Bonard Fowler in Marion on February 18, 1965, and died eight days later.

name: Cheri Jo Bates
summary: Cheri Jo Bates, 18, a Riverside City College freshman, was stabbed to death near the campus library on the night of October 30, 1966; her body was found the next morning.

name: Richard Speck Victims
summary: Richard Speck broke into a Chicago townhouse and methodically murdered eight student nurses. Corazon Amurao survived by hiding under a bed and later identified Speck.

name: Valerie Percy
summary: Valerie Percy, 21, daughter of U.S. Senate candidate Charles Percy, was beaten and stabbed in her bedroom at the family's lakefront home in Kenilworth, Illinois, early on September 18, 1966.

name: Barbara Jane Mackle
summary: Barbara Jane Mackle, 20, an Emory University student, was abducted at gunpoint from a Decatur, Georgia, motel on December 17, 1968, and buried in a ventilated box while a $500,000 ransom was demanded.

name: David Faraday & Betty Lou Jensen
summary: David Faraday, 17, and Betty Lou Jensen, 16, were shot with a .22-caliber pistol at a turnout on Lake Herman Road, just outside Benicia, California, late on December 20, 1968.

name: Jane Durrua
summary: Jane Durrua, 13, of Keansburg, New Jersey, disappeared on November 4, 1968, and was found dead in a field in Middletown the next morning.

name: Robert F. Kennedy Assassination
summary: Senator Robert F. Kennedy, 42, was shot in the kitchen pantry of the Ambassador Hotel in Los Angeles shortly after midnight on June 5, 1968, after winning the California Democratic primary; he died on June 6.

name: Zodiac Killer Victims
summary: At least five confirmed victims were killed by an unidentified serial killer in Northern California between 1968 and 1969. The killer taunted police and newspapers with cryptic letters and ciphers signed with a crosshair symbol.

name: Bryan Hartnell & Cecelia Shepard
summary: College students Cecelia Shepard, 22, and Bryan Hartnell, 20, were tied up and stabbed by a hooded man on the shore of Lake Berryessa in Napa County, California, on September 27, 1969.

name: Charles Manson Victims
summary: Charles Manson directed his followers to commit a series of brutal murders in Los Angeles on August 9-10, 1969, killing seven people including actress Sharon Tate.

name: Jane Britton
summary: Jane Britton, 23, a Harvard graduate student in anthropology, was sexually assaulted and beaten to death in her Cambridge apartment on January 7, 1969.

name: Mary Jo Kopechne
summary: Mary Jo Kopechne, 28, died when a car driven by Senator Edward Kennedy went off Dike Bridge into Poucha Pond on Chappaquiddick Island late on July 18, 1969. Her death was attributed to drowning.

name: Paul Stine
summary: Cab driver and graduate student Paul Lee Stine, 29, was shot in the head by a passenger at Washington and Cherry streets in San Francisco's Presidio Heights on October 11, 1969.

name: Dean Corll Victims
summary: Dean Corll, with accomplices David Brooks and Elmer Wayne Henley, tortured and murdered at least 28 young men and boys in Houston. Corll was shot and killed by Henley in 1973, who then led police to multiple burial sites.

name: Christine Marie Eastin
summary: Christine Marie Eastin, 19, vanished in Hayward, California, on the night of January 18, 1971, after driving her former boyfriend's blue 1969 Ford Maverick to a self-service car wash on Mission Boulevard.

name: D.B. Cooper
summary: A man calling himself Dan Cooper hijacked Northwest Orient Flight 305 in 1971, extorted $200,000 in ransom, and parachuted from the plane somewhere over the Pacific Northwest. He was never identified or found.

name: List Family Murders
summary: John List shot his wife, his mother and his three teenage children at their home in Westfield, New Jersey, on November 9, 1971, and disappeared. The bodies were found on December 7, 1971.

name: Robert Hansen Victims
summary: Robert Hansen was an Anchorage baker who abducted women, flew them to remote Alaska wilderness, and hunted them. He confessed to 17 murders and was convicted in 1984. He died in prison in 2014.

name: Texas Killing Fields Victims
summary: Since the early 1970s the bodies of more than 30 women and girls have been found along the Interstate 45 corridor between Houston and Galveston, including four found in a field off Calder Road in League City known as the Killing…

name: John Wayne Gacy Victims
summary: John Wayne Gacy tortured and murdered 33 young men and boys, burying 26 under his house. He was convicted in 1980 and executed in 1994. After his execution, investigators used DNA to identify unknown victims.

name: Barbara Gibbons
summary: Barbara Gibbons, 51, was killed in her home in the Falls Village section of Canaan, Connecticut, on September 28, 1973. Her son Peter Reilly, 18, was convicted of manslaughter in 1974 on the basis of a confession he recanted.

name: BTK Killer Victims
summary: Dennis Rader, known as BTK (Bind, Torture, Kill), murdered 10 people in and around Wichita, Kansas between 1974 and 1991. He taunted police and media for decades.

name: Coral Eugene Watts Victims
summary: Carl Eugene "Coral" Watts admitted killing about a dozen women in Texas and Michigan under a 1982 Texas plea deal that gave him immunity for those murders and a 60-year sentence for burglary with intent to murder.

name: Golden State Killer Victims

name: Margaret Ellen Fox
summary: Margaret Ellen Fox, 14, disappeared on June 24, 1974, after taking a bus from Burlington, New Jersey, to Mount Holly to meet a man who had answered her babysitting advertisement and called himself John Marshall.

name: Otero Family Murders
summary: Joseph and Julie Otero and two of their children, Josephine, 11, and Joseph II, 9, were killed in their Wichita home on January 15, 1974, the first murders by the offender who called himself BTK.

name: Patty Hearst Kidnapping
summary: Newspaper heiress Patty Hearst, 19, was abducted from her Berkeley apartment by the Symbionese Liberation Army on February 4, 1974.

name: Ted Bundy Victims
summary: Ted Bundy confessed to 30 homicides across seven states, though the actual number is believed higher. He was executed in Florida in 1989.

name: Ted Bundy Washington Victims
summary: Eight young women vanished in Washington and Oregon between February and July 1974, beginning with Lynda Ann Healy in Seattle. Remains of seven were later found near Issaquah and on Taylor Mountain; Donna Manson was never…

name: David Williams & Steven Anderson
summary: David Williams, 12, and his roommate Steven Anderson, 17, disappeared on April 7, 1975, from the New Lisbon State School, a residential center for people with developmental disabilities in Burlington County, New Jersey.

name: Jimmy Hoffa
summary: Former Teamsters Union president Jimmy Hoffa was last seen in a restaurant parking lot in Bloomfield Township, Michigan, on July 30, 1975.

name: Myrna Opsahl
summary: Myrna Opsahl, 42, was fatally shot on April 21, 1975, while depositing church collection money during a Symbionese Liberation Army robbery of the Crocker National Bank in Carmichael, California.

name: Robert Lee Yates Victims
summary: Robert Lee Yates Jr., a former Army helicopter pilot, pleaded guilty in 2000 to 13 murders committed in Washington between 1975 and 1998 and was sentenced to 408 years.

name: Anna Mae Aquash
summary: Anna Mae Pictou Aquash, a 30-year-old Mi'kmaq activist in the American Indian Movement, was shot in mid-December 1975; her body was found near Wanblee on the Pine Ridge Reservation on February 24, 1976.

name: Oakland County Child Killer Victims
summary: A serial killer known as the 'Babysitter' abducted and murdered four children in Oakland County, Michigan. The victims ranged in age from 10 to 12 years old.

name: Son of Sam Victims
summary: David Berkowitz, known as 'Son of Sam,' murdered six people and wounded seven others in New York City over 13 months. He terrorized the city with taunting letters to police and media.

name: Bonnie Garland
summary: Bonnie Garland, a 20-year-old Yale student, was fatally beaten with a hammer as she slept in her parents' Scarsdale, New York, home on July 7, 1977.

name: Hillside Strangler Victims
summary: Cousins Angelo Buono and Kenneth Bianchi posed as police officers, kidnapped, raped, and murdered 10 women in Los Angeles. Their victims were found on hillsides, giving rise to the 'Hillside Strangler' name.

name: Roger Kibbe Victims
summary: Roger Reece Kibbe, called the I-5 Strangler, was convicted of murdering seven women and girls in Northern California between 1977 and 1987.

name: Bob Crane
summary: Actor Bob Crane, 49, star of Hogan's Heroes, was found bludgeoned to death in his Scottsdale, Arizona, apartment on June 29, 1978. His friend John Carpenter was charged in 1992 and acquitted by a jury in 1994; he died in 1998.

name: FSU Chi Omega Murders
summary: Margaret Bowman, 21, and Lisa Levy, 20, were killed and two sorority sisters badly injured when Ted Bundy attacked the Chi Omega house at Florida State University early on January 15, 1978.

name: Jeffrey Dahmer Victims
summary: Jeffrey Dahmer murdered 17 young men and boys in Wisconsin and Ohio, engaging in necrophilia and cannibalism. He was convicted of 15 murders in Wisconsin and sentenced to 15 life terms.

name: Judy Chartier
summary: Judith "Judy" Chartier, 17, of Chelmsford, Massachusetts, vanished after leaving a party in Billerica around 2 a.m. on June 5, 1982.

name: Kimberly Leach
summary: Twelve-year-old Kimberly Leach was abducted from Lake City Junior High School in Florida on February 9, 1978. Her remains were found in April 1978 in a shed near Suwannee River State Park.

name: Rep. Leo Ryan & Jonestown Victims
summary: U.S. Congressman Leo Ryan was shot dead at the Port Kaituma airstrip in Guyana on November 18, 1978, along with four others, while investigating Jim Jones's Peoples Temple.

name: Frank Hilley
summary: Frank Hilley died on May 25, 1975, in a death first attributed to infectious hepatitis. After his daughter Carol was found to have been poisoned with arsenic in 1979, his body was exhumed and arsenic was detected.

name: Atlanta Child Murders Victims
summary: At least 28 young Black children and adults were murdered in Atlanta between 1979 and 1981, causing citywide panic. Wayne Williams was convicted of two adult murders and sentenced to life.

name: Etan Patz
summary: Six-year-old Etan Patz was one of the first missing children to appear on a milk carton when he disappeared walking to school in SoHo. The case transformed child safety in America.

name: Susan Reinert
summary: Teacher Susan Reinert of Ardmore was last seen on June 22, 1979; her body was found three days later in the trunk of her car at a hotel near Harrisburg. Her children, Karen, 11, and Michael, 10, were never found.

name: Betty Gore
summary: Betty Gore, 30, was killed with an axe at her home in Wylie, Texas, on June 13, 1980, sustaining 41 blows. Her friend Candy Montgomery was charged with murder and testified that she acted in self-defense after Gore confronted her.

name: Herman Tarnower
summary: Dr. Herman Tarnower, 69, author of the Scarsdale Diet, was shot dead at his home in Purchase, New York, on March 10, 1980, by his longtime companion Jean Harris.

name: Jeannie Mills Family
summary: Peoples Temple defectors Jeannie Mills, 40, and Al Mills, 51, were shot dead with their daughter Daphene, 15, at their Berkeley home on February 26, 1980. The couple had co-founded the Concerned Relatives group.

name: Tammy Terrell
summary: The body of a teenage girl found in the desert in Henderson, Nevada, on October 5, 1980, was identified in 2021 as Tammy Terrell, 17, of Roswell, New Mexico.

name: Adam Walsh
summary: Six-year-old Adam Walsh was abducted from a Sears store in Hollywood, Florida, on July 27, 1981. His severed head was found two weeks later.

name: Dean and Tina Clouse
summary: The remains of Harold Dean Clouse Jr. and his wife, Tina Linn Clouse, were found in woods in the Houston area on January 12, 1981, and were not identified until 2021 through genetic genealogy.

name: Keddie Cabin Murders
summary: Glenna "Sue" Sharp, her son John, and his friend Dana Wingate were bound, stabbed, and bludgeoned in Cabin 28 at the Keddie Resort on the night of April 11-12, 1981.

name: Marcia King (Buckskin Girl)
summary: Marcia King, 21, of Arkansas, was found strangled beside Greenlee Road near Troy, Ohio, on April 24, 1981. Unidentified for nearly 37 years, she was known as Buckskin Girl for her fringed jacket.

name: Philip Testa
summary: Philip "Chicken Man" Testa, 56, reputed head of the Philadelphia crime family, was fatally injured on March 15, 1981 when a nail-packed bomb exploded on the porch of his South Philadelphia home.

name: Sebastian Russo
summary: Dr. Sebastian Russo, 56, a Baltimore family physician known for charging patients $5 or less, was shot dead in his Harford Road office on the evening of February 27, 1981.

name: Tammy Mahoney
summary: Tammy Mahoney, a 19-year-old SUNY Morrisville student, vanished on May 8, 1981 after hitchhiking near Route 46 in Oneida, New York.

name: Chicago Tylenol Murders Victims
summary: Seven people in Chicago died after taking cyanide-laced Tylenol capsules in 1982. The deaths prompted a nationwide recall and led to tamper-resistant packaging regulations. James W.

name: Diane Suzuki
summary: Diane Suzuki, a 19-year-old University of Hawaii student, disappeared on July 6, 1985 from the Rosalie Woodson Dance Academy in Aiea, where she taught part-time. Her purse, keys and car were left behind.

name: Dorothea Puente Victims
summary: Dorothea Puente was a Sacramento boardinghouse operator who poisoned elderly tenants and continued cashing their Social Security checks. Seven bodies were found buried in her yard in 1988.

name: Green River Killer Victims
summary: Gary Ridgway, the Green River Killer, murdered at least 49 women in Washington State. He targeted mostly sex workers and runaways. Ridgway was convicted in 2003 after DNA evidence linked him to four victims.

name: Kathleen McCormack Durst
summary: Kathleen McCormack Durst, a 29-year-old medical student, disappeared on January 31, 1982 from South Salem, New York, and has never been found.

name: Kellie Poppleton
summary: Kellie Jean Poppleton, a 14-year-old Fremont student, was found dead beside Kilkare Road in Sunol, California on December 2, 1983. She had been beaten and strangled.

name: Wah Mee Club Massacre
summary: Thirteen people were robbed and murdered at the Wah Mee private gambling club in Seattle's Chinatown-International District on February 19, 1983; a fourteenth victim survived.

name: Angela Samota
summary: Angela Samota, a 20-year-old Southern Methodist University student, was raped and stabbed to death in her Dallas home in the early hours of October 13, 1984.

name: Night Stalker Victims
summary: Richard Ramirez, the Night Stalker, terrorized Southern California and the San Francisco Bay Area in 1984-1985 with a series of home-invasion murders, rapes, and burglaries.

name: Vicki Lynne Hoskinson
summary: Eight-year-old Vicki Lynne Hoskinson vanished on September 17, 1984 while riding her bicycle to mail a birthday card near her Tucson home. Her remains were found in the desert northwest of the city on April 12, 1985.

name: Grim Sleeper Victims
summary: Lonnie Franklin Jr., known as the Grim Sleeper, was convicted of killing 10 women in Los Angeles between 1985 and 2007. He appeared to stop killing for years (hence 'Grim Sleeper') and was identified through familial DNA from…

name: Shari Smith
summary: Seventeen-year-old Shari Faye Smith was abducted at gunpoint from the end of her family's driveway in Lexington County, South Carolina, on May 31, 1985, and her body was found days later in Saluda County.

name: Steve Christensen & Kathy Sheets
summary: Steven Christensen and Kathleen Sheets were killed by package pipe bombs in the Salt Lake City area on October 15, 1985. Document dealer Mark Hofmann, injured the next day when a third bomb exploded in his car, pleaded guilty in…

name: Anthonette Christine Cayedito
summary: Nine-year-old Anthonette Cayedito vanished from her family's apartment in Gallup, New Mexico, in the early hours of April 6, 1986, after going to answer a knock at the door.

name: Colonial Parkway Murders
summary: Eight young people were killed or disappeared in four incidents along or near Virginia's Colonial Parkway between 1986 and 1989.

name: Gary Heidnik Victims
summary: Gary Heidnik abducted six women between November 1986 and March 1987 and held them captive in the basement of his North Philadelphia home, where Sandra Lindsay and Deborah Dudley died.

name: Jennifer Levin
summary: Jennifer Levin, 18, was found strangled in Central Park behind the Metropolitan Museum of Art on August 26, 1986, hours after leaving an Upper East Side bar with Robert Chambers.

name: Lisa Steinberg
summary: Six-year-old Lisa Steinberg was fatally beaten on November 1, 1987, in the Greenwich Village apartment of Joel Steinberg, a lawyer who had raised her without ever legally adopting her.

name: Peggy Hettrick
summary: Peggy Hettrick, 37, was found stabbed and mutilated in a field in Fort Collins, Colorado, on February 11, 1987. Tim Masters, 15 at the time, was convicted in 1999, but the conviction was vacated in January 2008 after DNA testing…

name: Amber Swartz
summary: Seven-year-old Amber Swartz-Garcia vanished on June 3, 1988, while jumping rope in the front yard of her home in Pinole, California.

name: Tara Leigh Calico
summary: Nineteen-year-old Tara Calico went for a bike ride along Highway 47 and never returned. Her bicycle was never found. A year later, a polaroid photo of a bound young woman and boy was found at a Florida convenience store…

name: Aileen Wuornos Victims
summary: Aileen Wuornos killed seven men along Florida highways, claiming self-defense. She was convicted of six murders and executed in 2002.

name: Dan & Linda Broderick
summary: Attorney Daniel T. Broderick III, 44, and his wife Linda Kolkena Broderick, 28, were shot in their bed at their San Diego home on November 5, 1989, by his former wife, Betty Broderick.

name: Grissom Family Murders (Danny Rolling Confession)
summary: William "Tom" Grissom, 55, his daughter Julie, 24, and his grandson Sean, 8, were killed in their Shreveport home on November 4, 1989. Danny Rolling was long suspected but never charged in Louisiana.

name: Ilene Beth Misheloff
summary: Thirteen-year-old Ilene Misheloff vanished on January 30, 1989, while walking home from Wells Middle School in Dublin, California. She was last seen at about 3 p.m.

name: Jacob Wetterling
summary: Eleven-year-old Jacob Wetterling was abducted at gunpoint near his home in St. Joseph, Minnesota, on October 22, 1989. His disappearance led to the 1994 Jacob Wetterling Crimes Against Children and Sexually Violent Offender…

name: Lisa Bianco
summary: Lisa Bianco was beaten to death outside her Mishawaka, Indiana, home on March 4, 1989, by her former husband, Alan Matheney, who was on an eight-hour prison furlough. She had not been notified of his release.

name: Robert Ben Rhoades Victims

name: Gainesville Ripper Victims
summary: Danny Rolling murdered five college students over four days in Gainesville, Florida, in August 1990; four attended the University of Florida and one attended Santa Fe Community College.

name: Paige Marie Renkoski
summary: Paige Renkoski, a 30-year-old substitute teacher from Okemos, Michigan, vanished on May 24, 1990. The car she was driving was found still running on the shoulder of westbound I-96 near Fowlerville, with her purse and shoes inside.

name: Charles Albright Victims
summary: Charles Albright was convicted in December 1991 of murdering Shirley Williams, one of three women found shot in Dallas between December 1990 and March 1991 with their eyes removed.

name: Danny Casolaro
summary: Freelance journalist Joseph Daniel "Danny" Casolaro, 44, was found dead on August 10, 1991, in the bathtub of Room 517 at the Sheraton hotel in Martinsburg, West Virginia, with cuts to his wrists.

name: Latasha Harlins
summary: Latasha Harlins, 15, was shot in the back of the head by store owner Soon Ja Du at Empire Liquor Market in South Los Angeles on March 16, 1991, after a dispute over a bottle of orange juice.

name: Mark Himebaugh
summary: Eleven-year-old Mark Himebaugh disappeared on November 25, 1991, near his home on Sunray Road in Del Haven, Middle Township, New Jersey, after going to watch firefighters tackle a nearby brush fire.

name: I-70 Killer Victims
summary: Six store workers were shot dead at five small businesses near Interstate 70 in Indiana, Kansas and Missouri between April 8 and May 7, 1992.

name: Jeremy Guillory
summary: Six-year-old Jeremy Guillory was strangled on February 7, 1992, in a house near Iowa, Louisiana, where Ricky Langley rented a room.

name: Springfield Three
summary: Sherrill Levitt, her daughter Suzanne Streeter, and Suzanne's friend Stacy McCall all vanished from the Levitt home overnight. Their cars were still in the driveway, their purses inside. The porch light's glass globe was broken.

name: Holly Piirainen
summary: Ten-year-old Holly Piirainen disappeared on August 5, 1993, after leaving her grandparents' home in Sturbridge, Massachusetts, to see a neighbor's puppies. Hunters found her remains in Brimfield on October 23, 1993.

name: Polly Klaas
summary: Twelve-year-old Polly Klaas was kidnapped at knifepoint from a slumber party at her Petaluma home and murdered. Richard Allen Davis was convicted and sentenced to death.

name: Steve Branch, Michael Moore & Christopher Byers
summary: Three eight-year-old boys were murdered in West Memphis, Arkansas, in May 1993. Three teenagers — Damien Echols, Jason Baldwin, and Jessie Misskelley Jr.

name: Crystal Ann Tymich
summary: Six-year-old Crystal Ann Tymich disappeared on June 30, 1994, while playing outside near her home on Brynhurst Avenue in South Los Angeles.

name: Dr. John Bayard Britton
summary: Dr. John Britton, 69, and his volunteer escort James Barrett, 74, were shot dead outside the Ladies Center clinic in Pensacola, Florida, on July 29, 1994; Barrett's wife June was wounded.

name: Lamar Johnson (Exoneration)

name: Melissa Witt
summary: Nineteen-year-old Melissa Witt was abducted from the parking lot of the Bowling World bowling alley in Fort Smith, Arkansas, on December 1, 1994.

name: Nicole Brown Simpson & Ron Goldman

name: Fort Worth Missing Trio
summary: Mary Rachel Trlica, 17, Lisa Renee Wilson, 14, and Julie Ann Moseley, 9, disappeared on December 23, 1974, after going Christmas shopping at Seminary South Shopping Center in Fort Worth, Texas.

name: Cornelia Crilley
summary: Cornelia Crilley, a 23-year-old TWA flight attendant, was found strangled in her apartment on Manhattan's Upper East Side in June 1971.

name: Dee Dee Blanchard
summary: Dee Dee Blanchard was murdered by her daughter Gypsy Rose's boyfriend after years of medical child abuse (Munchausen syndrome by proxy). Gypsy had been forced to feign illness and disability her entire life.

name: Nipsey Hussle
summary: Grammy-nominated rapper and community activist Nipsey Hussle was shot and killed outside his Marathon Clothing store in the Hyde Park neighborhood of Los Angeles. Eric Holder Jr. was convicted of first-degree murder in 2022.

name: Daniel Morcombe
summary: Thirteen-year-old Daniel Morcombe disappeared while waiting for a bus at Woombye on Queensland's Sunshine Coast on December 7, 2003.

name: Sarah Everard
summary: Sarah Everard, 33, was kidnapped, raped and murdered by serving Metropolitan Police officer Wayne Couzens while walking home in south London on March 3, 2021.

name: Jenny Lin
summary: Fourteen-year-old Jenny Lin was stabbed to death in her family's home in Castro Valley, California, on May 27, 1994; her father found her in a bathroom when he returned from work.

name: Peter Falconio
summary: British backpacker Peter Falconio, 28, was shot on the Stuart Highway near Barrow Creek in Australia's Northern Territory on July 14, 2001; his girlfriend Joanne Lees escaped.

name: Brandy Hall
summary: Firefighter Brandy Hall vanished on August 17, 2006 after leaving the Malabar fire station in Brevard County, Florida, where she volunteered.

name: Emanuela Orlandi
summary: Fifteen-year-old Emanuela Orlandi, daughter of a Vatican employee, disappeared in Rome. Her case has been linked to theories involving the Vatican, organized crime, and international espionage.

name: Jayme Closs
summary: Thirteen-year-old Jayme Closs was kidnapped after her parents were murdered in Barron, Wisconsin. She escaped 88 days later. Jake Patterson was sentenced to life in prison.

name: Trevaline Evans
summary: Antiques dealer Trevaline Evans vanished from her shop in Llangollen, Wales, leaving a 'Back in 2 minutes' sign on the door. She was never seen again.

name: Phoenix Coldon
summary: Phoenix Coldon, a 23-year-old college student, was last seen on December 18, 2011, driving away from her family's home in Spanish Lake, Missouri. Her black 1998 Chevrolet Blazer was found abandoned in East St.

name: Dorothy Kilgallen
summary: Journalist Dorothy Kilgallen, who was investigating the JFK assassination, was found dead in her New York townhouse. Her death was ruled an overdose but many believe she was murdered.

name: Dagmar Hagelin
summary: Swedish-Argentine teenager Dagmar Hagelin, 17, was shot and abducted by an Argentine Navy task group in El Palomar, Buenos Aires Province, on January 27, 1977, and was last seen by fellow detainees at the ESMA detention centre.

name: Helen Brach
summary: Candy heiress Helen Brach vanished after a visit to the Mayo Clinic. Her disappearance was linked to a horse-related fraud ring. She was declared legally dead in 1984.

name: Barbara Bolick
summary: Barbara Bolick, 55, of Corvallis, Montana, disappeared on July 18, 2007 while hiking near Bear Creek Overlook in the Bitterroot Mountains outside Victor.

name: Nicole Morin
summary: Eight-year-old Nicole Morin disappeared from the hallway of her Toronto apartment building while on her way to the swimming pool. She has never been found.

name: Cecilia Zhang
summary: Nine-year-old Cecilia Zhang was kidnapped from her bedroom in Toronto. Her body was found five months later. Min Chen pleaded guilty to second-degree murder.

name: Daniel Morgan
summary: Private investigator Daniel Morgan, 37, was killed with an axe in the car park of the Golden Lion pub in Sydenham, south London, on March 10, 1987.

name: Marion Barter
summary: Australian schoolteacher Marion Barter secretly changed her name before vanishing during an overseas trip. She legally became 'Florabella Natalia Marion Remakel' before disappearing.

name: Patricia Adkins
summary: Patricia "Patti" Adkins, 29, has not been seen since she finished a late shift at the Honda plant in Marysville, Ohio, on June 29, 2001.

name: Angie Housman
summary: Nine-year-old Angie Housman was abducted after leaving her school bus in St. Ann, Missouri, on November 18, 1993. A hunter found her body nine days later in the Busch Wildlife Area in St. Charles County.

name: Mark Kilroy
summary: University of Texas student Mark Kilroy was kidnapped during spring break in Matamoros, Mexico and ritually murdered by a drug-trafficking cult. His remains were found at a ranch with other victims.

name: Meredith Kercher
summary: British exchange student Meredith Kercher, 21, was killed in her bedroom in Perugia, Italy, on November 1, 2007. Rudy Guede was convicted of murder and sexual assault in 2008 and released in 2021 after serving 13 years of a…

name: Deborah Waring
summary: Twenty-year-old Deborah Waring was found murdered in Goddard Memorial State Park in Warwick, Rhode Island. Her case is one of Rhode Island's oldest unsolved homicides.

name: Scott Johnson
summary: American mathematician Scott Johnson was found dead at the base of cliffs in Manly, Sydney. Initially ruled a suicide, his death was reclassified as a gay hate crime. Scott White pleaded guilty to manslaughter in 2023.

name: Suzanne Sevakis
summary: Suzanne Sevakis, 20, died in April 1990 five days after an apparent hit-and-run in Oklahoma City, where she was known as Tonya Hughes.

name: Katrice Lee
summary: Katrice Lee, the daughter of a British soldier, disappeared on her second birthday, November 28, 1981, from a NAAFI shopping complex at Schloss Neuhaus near Paderborn, West Germany.

name: Jill Meagher
summary: Jill Meagher, a 29-year-old Irish-born ABC Radio Melbourne employee, was raped and murdered while walking home along Sydney Road in Brunswick, Melbourne, in the early hours of September 22, 2012.

name: Lynette Dawson
summary: Lynette Dawson vanished from her Sydney home. Her husband Chris Dawson, a former rugby league player and teacher, was convicted of her murder in 2022 after the podcast 'The Teacher's Pet' revived interest.

name: Nell Cropsey
summary: Nineteen-year-old Nell Cropsey vanished from her family home in Elizabeth City, North Carolina. Her body was found in the Pasquotank River 37 days later. Her beau Jim Wilcox was convicted but later pardoned.

name: Christopher Kerze
summary: Christopher Kerze, 17, has been missing since April 20, 1990, when he left his family's home in Eagan, Minnesota, in the family van.

name: Claudia Kirschhoch
summary: Claudia Kirschhoch, a 29-year-old New York travel writer and editor with Frommer's Travel Guides, disappeared in Negril, Jamaica, in late May 2000 after a press trip to Cuba was cancelled.

name: Barbara Blatnik
summary: Barbara Blatnik, 17, of Garfield Heights, Ohio, was found strangled beside O'Neil Road in Cuyahoga Falls on December 20, 1987. In May 2020, after DNA and genetic genealogy work funded by the Porchlight Project, police arrested…

name: Robert Pickton Victims
summary: Robert Pickton, a pig farmer from Port Coquitlam, British Columbia, was convicted in December 2007 of the second-degree murders of six women and sentenced to life in prison. Police began searching his farm on February 5, 2002.

name: Tina Smith
summary: Tina Smith, 41, was found dead in her Roanoke County, Virginia home on December 6, 2010, and her 12-year-old daughter was missing.

name: Dorothy Jane Scott
summary: Dorothy Jane Scott, 32, vanished from the parking lot of UC Irvine Medical Center in Orange County, California, on the night of May 28, 1980, after months of anonymous calls from a man who alternately professed love and…

name: Amy Lord
summary: Twenty-four-year-old Amy Lord was kidnapped from her South Boston apartment, forced to withdraw money from ATMs, then murdered. Edwin Alemany was convicted and sentenced to life.

name: Vanessa Guillen
summary: Army specialist Vanessa Guillen was bludgeoned to death by fellow soldier Aaron Robinson at Fort Hood. The case exposed systemic failures in military sexual harassment reporting.

name: Ann Marie Burr
summary: Eight-year-old Ann Marie Burr vanished from her Tacoma, Washington home. Serial killer Ted Bundy, who lived nearby as a teenager, has been speculated as a suspect but the connection was never proven.

name: Gannon Stauch
summary: Gannon Stauch, 11, was reported missing from his home near Colorado Springs on January 27, 2020; his remains were found in Florida that March.

name: Pamela Butler
summary: Pamela Butler, a 47-year-old Environmental Protection Agency analyst, vanished from her Washington, D.C. home in February 2009. Her boyfriend Jose Rodriguez-Cruz was arrested in 2017, pleaded guilty to second-degree murder and…

name: Lori Hacking
summary: Lori Hacking, 27, was shot at her Salt Lake City apartment on July 19, 2004 by her husband, Mark Hacking, who reported her missing the same morning. He had invented a college degree and a medical school place.

name: Niqui McCown
summary: Marilyn "Niqui" McCown, 28, disappeared on July 22, 2001 in Richmond, Indiana, after doing laundry and stopping at a convenience store, three weeks before her wedding.

name: Karen Mitchell
summary: Sixteen-year-old Karen Mitchell vanished on November 25, 1997 after leaving the Bayshore Mall in Eureka, California on foot. Authorities believe she was abducted; she has never been found and no one has been charged.

name: Leigh Matthews
summary: Leigh Matthews, a 21-year-old student, was kidnapped from the Bond University campus parking lot in Johannesburg on July 9, 2004.

name: Erica Parsons
summary: Erica Parsons, 13, of Rowan County, North Carolina, died in December 2011 but was not reported missing until July 30, 2013. Her remains were found near Pageland, South Carolina, in September 2016.

name: Shannan Gilbert
summary: Shannan Gilbert disappeared at Oak Beach, Long Island on May 1, 2010; the search for her led to the discovery of the Gilgo Beach victims. Her remains were found in December 2011 and her cause of death is officially undetermined.

name: Lena Chapin
summary: Lena Chapin, 20, was last seen on February 14, 2006, at her apartment outside Steelville, Missouri. Relatives say she had described witnessing the 1999 death of her stepfather, Gary McCullough, who is also missing.

name: Sandra Cantu
summary: Eight-year-old Sandra Cantu disappeared from the Orchard Estates Mobile Home Park in Tracy, California, on March 27, 2009. Her body was found ten days later in a suitcase in an irrigation pond.

name: Ahmaud Arbery
summary: Ahmaud Arbery was chased and shot dead while jogging in Brunswick, Georgia by three white men. The case sparked national outrage over racial violence. All three were convicted of murder.

name: Kelsey Berreth
summary: Pilot and flight instructor Kelsey Berreth was murdered on Thanksgiving Day by her fiancé Patrick Frazee in Woodland Park, Colorado. He burned her body. Frazee was sentenced to life.

name: Dylan Redwine
summary: Thirteen-year-old Dylan Redwine disappeared during a court-ordered visit with his father Mark in Bayfield, Colorado. Mark Redwine was convicted of his murder in 2021.

name: Heather Elvis
summary: Heather Elvis, 20, disappeared in Horry County, South Carolina, on December 18, 2013; her car was found at Peachtree Landing. Tammy Moorer (October 2018) and Sidney Moorer (September 2019) were each convicted of kidnapping and…

name: Alissa Turney
summary: Alissa Turney, 17, disappeared in Phoenix on May 17, 2001, the last day of her junior year at Paradise Valley High School, and has never been found. Her stepfather, Michael Turney, was charged with second-degree murder in 2020.

name: Brian Carrick
summary: Brian Carrick, 17, vanished on December 20, 2002 after walking into Val's Foods, the Johnsburg, Illinois grocery store where he worked. His blood was found in and around a produce cooler, but his body has never been located.

name: Holly Branagan
summary: Seventeen-year-old Moira "Holly" Branagan was stabbed to death in the kitchen of her family's home on Pine Top Trail in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, on March 28, 1979.

name: Sierah Joughin
summary: Twenty-year-old Sierah Joughin was abducted while bicycling in rural Ohio. James Worley, a convicted kidnapper, was convicted of her murder and sentenced to death.

name: Mary Agnes Moroney
summary: Two-year-old Mary Agnes Moroney was taken from her family's South Side Chicago apartment on May 15, 1930 by a woman using the name Julia Otis and was never returned.

name: Rui Pedro
summary: Eleven-year-old Rui Pedro Teixeira Mendonça disappeared from Lousada, Portugal on March 4, 1998. Afonso Dias, acquitted at a first trial in 2012, was later convicted of kidnapping and sentenced to three years in prison; he was…

name: Cheryl Grimmer
summary: Three-year-old Cheryl Grimmer was taken from outside the shower block at Fairy Meadow Beach, Wollongong, on January 12, 1970. A man was charged in 2017, but prosecutors dropped the case in 2019 after his 1971 confession, made as…

name: Haleigh Cummings
summary: Five-year-old Haleigh Cummings was last seen on the evening of February 9, 2009, at her father's mobile home in Satsuma, Florida, and was reported missing early the next morning.

name: Elsie Paroubek
summary: Elsie Paroubek, a Chicago girl of four or five, disappeared on April 8, 1911, while walking to her aunt's house. A month later her body was recovered from the drainage canal near Lockport, about 35 miles away.

name: Lacey Fletcher
summary: Lacey Fletcher, 36, was found dead on January 3, 2022 on a couch in her parents' home in Slaughter, Louisiana, after years of severe neglect.

name: Carol Stuart
summary: Carol Stuart, 30 and pregnant, was shot in a car in Boston's Mission Hill on October 23, 1989 and died the next morning; her son, delivered by caesarean, lived 17 days. Her husband Charles blamed a Black gunman.

name: Kathleen Peterson
summary: Kathleen Peterson, 48, was found dead at the foot of a staircase in her Durham, North Carolina, home on December 9, 2001. Her husband, novelist Michael Peterson, said she fell; he was convicted of first-degree murder in 2003…

name: Holly Maddux
summary: Helen "Holly" Maddux, 30, was last seen in Philadelphia on September 9, 1977; her body was found in March 1979 in a trunk in the apartment of her former partner, Ira Einhorn.

name: Susan Berman, Kathleen Durst & Morris Black
summary: Writer Susan Berman, 55, was found shot in her Los Angeles home on December 24, 2000. A jury convicted real estate heir Robert Durst of her murder in 2021, but the conviction was vacated after he died in January 2022 with an…

name: Sarah Stern
summary: Sarah Stern, 19, was strangled at her Neptune City, New Jersey, home on December 2, 2016, during a robbery, and her body was thrown from the Route 35 bridge; it has never been recovered.

name: Macin Smith
summary: Seventeen-year-old Macin Smith left his family's home in St. George, Utah, on the morning of September 1, 2015, and did not arrive at Desert Hills High School.

name: Joey Lynn Offutt
summary: Joey Lynn Offutt, 33, was found to be missing on July 12, 2007, when a deliberately set fire destroyed her home in Sykesville, Pennsylvania, and the body of her six-week-old son was found inside.

name: Madeline Kingsbury
summary: Madeline Kingsbury, 26, disappeared on March 31, 2023, after dropping her two children at daycare in Winona, Minnesota. Her remains were found on June 7, 2023, near Mabel in Fillmore County.

name: Mary Boyle
summary: Six-year-old Mary Boyle disappeared on March 18, 1977, near her grandparents' farm at Cashelard, outside Ballyshannon, County Donegal, Ireland.

name: Anne Marie Fahey
summary: Delaware Governor's scheduling secretary Anne Marie Fahey was murdered by her lover Thomas Capano, a prominent attorney. He disposed of her body at sea. Capano was sentenced to death.

name: Lisa Ziegert
summary: Lisa Ziegert, 24, who worked at a middle school, was abducted from her evening job at a card shop in Agawam, Massachusetts, on April 15, 1992, and found dead four days later.

name: Sophie Sergie
summary: Sophie Sergie, 20, of Pitkas Point, Alaska, was found sexually assaulted, stabbed and shot in a dormitory bathroom at the University of Alaska Fairbanks on April 26, 1993.

name: Wayne Nance Victims
summary: Wayne Nance, a Missoula furniture mover, is suspected by investigators of at least six killings in western Montana between 1974 and 1985.

name: Jessica Dishon
summary: Jessica Dishon, 17, vanished from her family's driveway in Bullitt County, Kentucky, on the morning of September 10, 1999, and was found beaten and strangled 17 days later.

name: Lisa Stebic
summary: Lisa Stebic, a 37-year-old mother of two, was last seen at her home in Plainfield, Illinois, on the evening of April 30, 2007, while she and her husband were divorcing. Her phone and credit cards were never used again.

name: Patrick Warren Sr.
summary: Patrick Warren Sr., 52, was shot and killed by Killeen, Texas police officer Reynaldo Contreras on January 10, 2021, after his family called for help during a mental health crisis.

name: Charles Morgan
summary: Escrow company president Charles Morgan was found shot dead in the desert near Tucson wearing a bulletproof vest and with a map to a motel. He had reported being stalked and had painted his car to avoid detection.

name: Jennifer Servo
summary: Television reporter Jennifer Servo, 22, was found dead in her Abilene, Texas, apartment on September 18, 2002, two days after she was killed.

name: Damon and Devon Routier
summary: Brothers Devon Routier, 6, and Damon Routier, 5, were fatally stabbed in their home in Rowlett, Texas, on June 6, 1996. Their mother, Darlie Routier, who said an intruder attacked them, was convicted of capital murder in Damon's…

name: Israel Keyes Victims
summary: Israel Keyes confessed to killing Samantha Koenig, 18, abducted in Anchorage on February 1, 2012, and Bill and Lorraine Currier, who vanished from Essex, Vermont, in June 2011.

name: Jennifer Pan
summary: Bich Ha Pan was shot dead and her husband Hann Pan badly wounded in a staged home invasion at their Markham, Ontario home on November 8, 2010.

name: Karla Brown
summary: Karla Brown, 22, was found dead in the basement of the Wood River, Illinois, house she had moved into the day before, on June 21, 1978.

name: Mary Day
summary: Mary Louise Day, 13, vanished from her family's home in Seaside, California, in the summer of 1981 and was not reported missing for more than a decade. Police opened a suspected homicide inquiry in 2002.

name: Adea Shabani
summary: Acting student Adea Shabani, 25, was last seen leaving her Hollywood apartment on February 23, 2018. Her remains were recovered a month later from a shallow grave in the Spenceville Wildlife Area in Nevada County, California…

name: Ashley Ellerin
summary: Michael Gargiulo was convicted in August 2019 of murdering Ashley Ellerin, a 22-year-old fashion design student who was stabbed 47 times in her Hollywood home on February 21, 2001.

name: Brittney Wood
summary: Nineteen-year-old Brittney Wood vanished while on her way to meet her uncle in Mobile, Alabama. The investigation uncovered a massive family sexual abuse ring. Brittney has never been found.

name: Cieha Taylor
summary: Cieha Taylor, 28, was last seen about 4 p.m. on February 6, 2020 in Plant City, Florida, after dropping her boyfriend at a home on Cowart Road.

name: Girly Chew Hossencofft
summary: Girly Chew Hossencofft disappeared from Albuquerque in 1999 during a divorce from her husband Diazien, who claimed to be a government scientist with alien DNA.

name: Jessie Davis
summary: Jessie Davis, 26 and nearly nine months pregnant, was killed at her home in Lake Township, Stark County, Ohio, on June 14, 2007. Her body was found nine days later in a Summit County park.

name: Sherin Mathews
summary: Three-year-old adopted Indian girl Sherin Mathews was reported missing in Richardson, Texas. Her adoptive father Wesley Mathews later admitted to killing her. He was sentenced to life.

name: Lina Sardar Khil
summary: Lina Sardar Khil, 3, disappeared on December 20, 2021, from the playground of the Villas Del Cabo apartment complex in San Antonio, Texas, where her family, who had come from Afghanistan, was living.

name: Amina and Sarah Said
summary: Sisters Amina Said, 18, and Sarah Said, 17, were found shot to death in a taxi outside a hotel in Irving, Texas, on January 1, 2008.

name: Karlie Gusé
summary: Sixteen-year-old Karlie Lain Gusé disappeared from her family's home in Chalfant, Mono County, California, early on October 13, 2018, after a night of paranoia that followed smoking marijuana at a party.

name: Katelin Akens
summary: Katelin Akens, 19, vanished on December 5, 2015, after being dropped at her former stepfather's home in Partlow, Spotsylvania County, Virginia, for a ride toward a flight to Arizona.

name: Flora Fire Victims
summary: Four sisters aged 5 to 11 - Keyana Davis, Keyara Phillips, Kerriele McDonald and Kionnie Welch - died in a house fire in Flora, Indiana, on November 21, 2016. Indiana State Police say the fire was intentionally set.

name: Claremont Serial Murders
summary: Three women vanished from the upscale suburb of Claremont in Perth, Australia between 1996-1997. Telstra technician Bradley Edwards was convicted of two murders in 2020.

name: Saronno Hospital Patient Deaths (Leonardo Cazzaniga case)
summary: Leonardo Cazzaniga, a former deputy head of the emergency department at Saronno Hospital in Lombardy, Italy, was convicted of killing patients with overdoses of morphine, anaesthetics and sedatives.

name: Michael & Alex Smith
summary: Michael Smith, 3, and his brother Alex, 14 months, drowned on October 25, 1994 when their mother, Susan Smith, let her car roll into John D. Long Lake near Union, South Carolina, with the boys strapped inside.

name: Yates Children
summary: Five children of the Yates family, aged six months to seven years, were drowned by their mother, Andrea Yates, at their home in the Clear Lake area of Houston on June 20, 2001.

name: Teresa Sievers
summary: Dr. Teresa Sievers, 46, was beaten to death with hammers in her Bonita Springs, Florida home on June 28, 2015. Her husband, Mark Sievers, was convicted of first-degree murder in December 2019 and sentenced to death.

name: Tamla Horsford
summary: Tamla Horsford, a Black mother of five, was found dead at a sleepover party at a white friend's home in Cumming, Georgia. Her death was ruled accidental but her family disputes this.

name: Emma Walker
summary: Sixteen-year-old Emma Walker was fatally shot in her bed at her family's Knoxville, Tennessee, home on November 21, 2016, by shots fired through her bedroom wall from outside.

name: Katelyn Markham
summary: Katelyn Markham, 21, disappeared from her home in Fairfield, Ohio, in August 2011; her skeletal remains were found in April 2013 in Cedar Grove, Indiana, and her death was ruled a homicide.

name: Tammy Daybell
summary: Tammy Daybell died at her home in Salem, Idaho on October 19, 2019. A coroner ruled the death natural without an autopsy, but her body was exhumed that December and an autopsy found she died of asphyxiation.

name: Maggie & Paul Murdaugh
summary: Maggie Murdaugh, 52, and her son Paul, 22, were shot dead at the family's hunting estate in Islandton, South Carolina, on June 7, 2021.

name: Harmony Montgomery
summary: Five-year-old Harmony Montgomery is believed to have died in Manchester, New Hampshire, in December 2019 but was not reported missing until late 2021; her remains have not been found.

name: Doerman Children
summary: Brothers Clayton, 7, Hunter, 4, and Chase Doerman, 3, were shot dead at their home in Monroe Township, Clermont County, Ohio, on June 15, 2023.

name: Eric Richins
summary: Eric Richins, 39, died of a fentanyl overdose at his home in Kamas, Utah on March 4, 2022. His wife Kouri Richins, who later published a children's book about grief, was convicted of aggravated murder in March 2026 and sentenced…

name: Ruby Franke Children
summary: Parenting YouTuber Ruby Franke and her business partner, counselor Jodi Hildebrandt, each pleaded guilty in December 2023 to four counts of aggravated child abuse of two of Franke's children.

name: Eliza Fletcher
summary: Teacher and heiress Eliza Fletcher was abducted while jogging near the University of Memphis and murdered. Cleotha Abston, who had a prior kidnapping conviction, was sentenced to life.

name: Orsolya Gaal
summary: Orsolya Gaal, 51, was stabbed more than 50 times in her Forest Hills, Queens home on April 16, 2022, and her body was left in a hockey duffel bag near Forest Park.

name: Sandy Hook Victims
summary: Twenty first-grade students and six educators were shot dead at Sandy Hook Elementary School in Newtown, Connecticut, on December 14, 2012.

name: Parkland Shooting Victims
summary: Nikolas Cruz killed 17 people and wounded 17 others at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland, Florida. He was sentenced to life without parole.

name: Mary Lou Morris
summary: Mary Lou Henderson Morris, 48, was found dead in her burned car near her Baytown, Texas, home on October 12, 2000. Days later, an unrelated Houston-area woman, Mary McGinnis Morris, 39, was found shot in her car.

name: Tristan Brübach
summary: Thirteen-year-old Tristan Brübach was brutally murdered in an underground pedestrian passage in Frankfurt, Germany. The case remains one of Germany's most notorious unsolved child murders.

name: Maleah Davis
summary: Four-year-old Maleah Davis was reported missing in Houston in May 2019 by her mother's ex-fiance Derion Vence, who claimed she was abducted during a carjacking.

name: Tyler Hadley Victims
summary: Seventeen-year-old Tyler Hadley bludgeoned his parents to death with a hammer, hid their bodies in a bedroom, and then hosted a house party. He was sentenced to life.

name: Trudy Appleby
summary: Eleven-year-old Trudy Appleby vanished from Moline, Illinois on August 21, 1996; her body has never been found. In August 2025 a Henry County grand jury indicted Jamison Fisher, a long-named person of interest, on first-degree…

name: Bianca Devins
summary: Seventeen-year-old Bianca Devins of Utica, New York, was killed on July 14, 2019 by Brandon Clark, 21, who had driven her home from a concert in New York City.

name: Rachel & Lillian Entwistle
summary: Rachel Entwistle, 27, and her nine-month-old daughter Lillian Rose were shot dead in their rented home in Hopkinton, Massachusetts, on January 20, 2006; police found them two days later.

name: Savannah Spurlock
summary: Savannah Spurlock, a Madison County, Kentucky, mother of four, disappeared after leaving a Lexington bar with three men on the night of January 4, 2019.

name: Evelyn Boswell
summary: Fifteen-month-old Evelyn Mae Boswell of Sullivan County, Tennessee, was reported missing on February 18, 2020, about two months after she was last seen.

name: Daniel Holtzclaw Victims
summary: Oklahoma City police officer Daniel Holtzclaw was convicted on December 10, 2015, of 18 of 36 counts, including four of first-degree rape, for sexually assaulting eight Black women while on patrol.

name: Lauren Smith-Fields
summary: Lauren Smith-Fields, 23, was found dead in her Bridgeport, Connecticut apartment on December 12, 2021 after a first date with a man she met on a dating app.

name: Shanquella Robinson
summary: Twenty-five-year-old Shanquella Robinson died on a group trip to Cabo San Lucas, Mexico. Video showed her being beaten by a friend. Her death was ruled homicide but no extradition has occurred.

name: Hart Family
summary: Six adopted children aged 12 to 19 died on March 26, 2018, when Jennifer Hart drove the family's SUV off a cliff on Highway 1 near Westport, California, with her wife Sarah also inside.

name: Gloria Satterfield
summary: Murdaugh family housekeeper Gloria Satterfield died after a fall at the Murdaugh home. Alex Murdaugh collected $4.3 million in insurance but stole the money from her sons.

name: Don Lewis
summary: Millionaire exotic animal owner Don Lewis vanished in Tampa, Florida on August 18, 1997 and was declared legally dead in 2002. The Netflix series 'Tiger King' revived interest in the case and aired accusations against his wife…

name: Mallory Beach
summary: Mallory Beach, 19, died when a boat carrying six young people struck a bridge at Archers Creek near Beaufort, South Carolina, early on February 24, 2019. Her body was found on March 3.

name: Dena Dean
summary: Fifteen-year-old Dena Dean was found stabbed to death in a park in Tamworth, England on her way to school. Despite extensive investigation, her killer has never been identified.

name: Jorge Torres Jr.
summary: Jorge Torres Jr. was found dead inside a suitcase in Winter Park, Florida. His girlfriend Sarah Boone claimed he died during a hide-and-seek game. She filmed him begging to be let out.

name: RJR Maintenance Murders
summary: Four people were murdered at RJR Maintenance in Mandan, North Dakota. Chiropractor Chad Isaak, a tenant of the property management company, was convicted after his car was caught on surveillance.

name: Jordan Neely
summary: Jordan Neely, a 30-year-old homeless man experiencing a mental health crisis on a New York City subway train, died after being placed in a chokehold by fellow passenger Daniel Penny on May 1, 2023.

name: Daniel Brophy
summary: Chef Daniel Brophy was murdered at the Oregon Culinary Institute. His wife Nancy, a romance novelist who wrote an essay called 'How to Murder Your Husband,' was convicted of his murder.

name: Nikki Kuhnhausen
summary: Seventeen-year-old transgender girl Nikki Kuhnhausen was killed in June 2019 by David Bogdanov after he learned she was transgender. Her remains were found on Larch Mountain in Clark County six months later.

name: Dayton Shooting
summary: Nine people were killed and 17 wounded by gunfire when Connor Betts, 24, opened fire in Dayton's Oregon District at about 1:05 a.m. on August 4, 2019.

name: Joel & Lisa Guy Sr.
summary: Joel Guy Sr., 61, and Lisa Guy, 55, were stabbed to death and dismembered at their home in west Knox County, Tennessee, over Thanksgiving weekend 2016.

name: Stephen Smith
summary: Nineteen-year-old Stephen Smith was found dead on a rural Hampton County road in July 2015. His death was initially treated as a hit-and-run, though no vehicle debris was found.

name: Russell Williams Victims
summary: Col. Russell Williams, commander of Canadian Forces Base Trenton, pleaded guilty in October 2010 to the first-degree murders of Cpl.

name: Peter Nygard Victims
summary: Fashion mogul Peter Nygard was arrested for racketeering and sex trafficking charges involving dozens of women. He was convicted in Canadian courts of sexual assault.

name: Derrick Todd Lee Victims
summary: Derrick Todd Lee was convicted in 2004 of murdering Geralyn DeSoto and Charlotte Murray Pace and was sentenced to death for the Pace killing.

name: Waneta Hoyt Children
summary: Waneta Hoyt murdered her five children between 1965 and 1971, presenting each death as SIDS. Her case was cited in medical literature supporting SIDS research before the truth emerged.

name: Yingying Zhang
summary: Yingying Zhang, a 26-year-old visiting scholar from China at the University of Illinois, was abducted from a bus stop in Urbana on June 9, 2017, and killed.

name: Jun Lin
summary: Luka Magnotta murdered Chinese international student Jun Lin in Montreal, dismembered him, and mailed body parts to political offices. He fled internationally before being caught in Berlin.

name: Stephen Port Victims
summary: Serial killer Stephen Port drugged and raped young men using GHB, killing four in Barking, East London. Police initially failed to link the deaths despite bodies being found in similar locations.

name: Yorkshire Ripper (death)
summary: Peter Sutcliffe, the Yorkshire Ripper who murdered 13 women in northern England, died of COVID-19 in prison in November 2020 after refusing treatment. He had served 39 years.

name: Grace Millane
summary: British backpacker Grace Millane was strangled in a central Auckland hotel apartment on the night of December 1-2, 2018, the eve of her 22nd birthday, after a date with a man she met on Tinder.

name: Ivan Milat (Backpacker Murders)
summary: Seven backpackers aged 19 to 22, from Australia, Germany and Britain, disappeared while hitchhiking from Sydney between December 1989 and April 1992; their bodies were found in the Belanglo State Forest in 1992 and 1993.

name: Cleo Smith
summary: Four-year-old Cleo Smith was taken from her family's tent at the Blowholes campsite north of Carnarvon, Western Australia, on October 16, 2021. Police found her alive 18 days later, on November 3, in a locked house in Carnarvon.

name: April Jones
summary: Mark Bridger was convicted on 30 May 2013 of abducting and murdering five-year-old April Jones, who was taken from the Bryn-y-Gog estate in Machynlleth, Wales, on 1 October 2012. He received a whole-life order at Mold Crown Court.

name: Jennifer Laude
summary: Transgender Filipina Jennifer Laude was murdered by U.S. Marine Joseph Scott Pemberton in a motel in Olongapo. The case strained U.S.-Philippine relations and sparked debate about the Visiting Forces Agreement.

name: Otto Warmbier
summary: American student Otto Warmbier was detained in North Korea for 17 months and returned to the U.S. in a vegetative state. He died days later. North Korea claimed he contracted botulism.

name: Jamal Khashoggi
summary: Saudi journalist Jamal Khashoggi was killed and dismembered inside the Saudi consulate in Istanbul by a team of Saudi agents. Eight people were convicted in a closed Saudi trial. A declassified 2021 U.S.

name: Alexander Litvinenko
summary: Former Russian spy Alexander Litvinenko was poisoned with polonium-210 in London. A British inquiry concluded Russian President Putin probably approved the operation. Two suspects were identified.

name: Sergei & Yulia Skripal Poisoning
summary: Former Russian double agent Sergei Skripal and his daughter Yulia were poisoned with Novichok nerve agent in Salisbury, England, and both survived; Dawn Sturgess died in July 2018 after handling the discarded agent.

name: Junko Furuta
summary: Junko Furuta, a 17-year-old high school student from Misato, Saitama, was abducted on November 25, 1988, and held for about 40 days in a house in Adachi, Tokyo, where she died on January 4, 1989.

name: Natascha Kampusch
summary: Ten-year-old Natascha Kampusch was kidnapped on her way to school in Vienna and held captive by Wolfgang Priklopil for over eight years in a basement dungeon. She escaped in 2006.

name: Peter & Joan Porco
summary: Chris Porco attacked his parents with an axe while they slept in Delmar, New York. His father died; his mother survived but lost an eye. Joan initially identified Chris by nodding, then denied it.

name: Donnah Winger
summary: Mark Winger murdered his wife Donnah and a shuttle driver he lured to their home, staging it to look like a break-in. He was a hero until a friend went to police years later.

name: Joe Andriano
summary: Joe Andriano, who was terminally ill with cancer, was killed in his Phoenix apartment on October 8, 2000. He had been struck at least 23 times on the head and stabbed in the neck, and sodium azide was found in his blood.

name: Liam Fee
summary: Two-year-old Liam Fee died at his home near Glenrothes, Fife, Scotland, on March 22, 2014, from heart injuries caused by blunt force trauma.

name: Daniel Pelka
summary: Daniel Pelka, 4, died of a head injury on March 3, 2012, in Coventry, England, after months of starvation and beatings. His mother, Magdalena Luczak, and her partner, Mariusz Krezolek, were convicted of murder at Birmingham…

name: Marc Dutroux Victims
summary: Six girls aged 8 to 19 were abducted in Belgium in 1995 and 1996; four died and two were rescued alive from a hidden cellar on August 15, 1996, two days after Marc Dutroux was arrested.

name: Josef Fritzl Case
summary: Josef Fritzl imprisoned his daughter Elisabeth in a cellar for 24 years, fathering seven children with her. The case was discovered in 2008 when one of the children needed hospital care.

name: Reeva Steenkamp
summary: Paralympic champion Oscar Pistorius shot and killed his girlfriend Reeva Steenkamp through a locked bathroom door on Valentine's Day. He claimed he thought she was an intruder. He was convicted of murder.

name: Madeline Soto
summary: Thirteen-year-old Madeline Soto was killed in Kissimmee, Florida, in February 2024 by her mother's boyfriend, Stephan Sterns, who had sexually abused her for years.

name: Laken Riley
summary: Laken Riley, a 22-year-old Augusta University nursing student, was killed on February 22, 2024 while running on a trail on the University of Georgia campus in Athens.

name: Rachel Morin
summary: Rachel Morin, a 37-year-old mother of five, was raped and murdered on the Ma & Pa Trail in Bel Air, Maryland, on August 5, 2023; her body was found the next day.

name: Audrii Cunningham
summary: Eleven-year-old Audrii Cunningham of Livingston, Texas, disappeared on February 15, 2024, after failing to board her school bus. Her body was recovered from the Trinity River five days later.

name: Ruby Garcia
summary: Ruby Garcia, 25, was shot and left beside southbound US-131 in Grand Rapids, Michigan, on March 22, 2024. Her boyfriend, Brandon Ortiz-Vite, pleaded guilty in September 2024 to second-degree murder and other charges.

name: Elijah Vue
summary: Three-year-old Elijah Vue was reported missing from Two Rivers, Wisconsin, on February 20, 2024, and his remains were found in a wooded area on September 7, 2024.

name: King Von
summary: Chicago rapper King Von (Dayvon Bennett), 26, was fatally shot outside the Monaco Hookah Lounge in Atlanta on November 6, 2020, when an argument between two groups turned into a gunfight.

name: XXXTentacion
summary: Rapper XXXTentacion (Jahseh Onfroy), 20, was shot and killed during a robbery outside RIVA Motorsports in Deerfield Beach, Florida, on June 18, 2018.

name: Pop Smoke
summary: Rapper Pop Smoke (Bashar Barakah Jackson), 20, was shot dead during a home-invasion robbery at a rented house in the Hollywood Hills on February 19, 2020.

name: Young Dolph
summary: Memphis rapper Young Dolph (Adolph Thornton Jr.), 36, was shot dead outside Makeda's Homemade Butter Cookies in Memphis on November 17, 2021.

name: Paul Bernardo & Karla Homolka Victims
summary: Paul Bernardo and Karla Homolka, the 'Ken and Barbie Killers,' raped and murdered teenagers Leslie Mahaffy and Kristen French in Ontario. Homolka received a controversial plea deal.

name: Clifford Olson Victims
summary: Clifford Olson murdered 11 children and young people, aged 9 to 18, in the Greater Vancouver area of British Columbia between November 1980 and July 1981.

name: Annecy Knife Attack
summary: A man stabbed six people, including four toddlers, at a lakeside playground in Annecy, France, in June 2023. All survived. The suspect, Abdalmasih Hanoun, a Syrian refugee who had been living in Sweden, was charged with…

name: Pedro López (Monster of the Andes)
summary: Colombian-born Pedro Alonso López was arrested in Ambato, Ecuador in 1980 and confessed to killing several hundred girls in Colombia, Ecuador and Peru.

name: Tsutomu Miyazaki Victims
summary: Tsutomu Miyazaki, the 'Otaku Killer,' murdered four young girls in the Tokyo/Saitama area. He kept body parts as trophies and sent taunting letters to families. He was executed in 2008.

name: Casey White (murder conviction)
summary: Connie Ridgeway, 59, was found stabbed to death in her Lauderdale County, Alabama apartment in October 2015. Inmate Casey White confessed in 2020 and was charged with capital murder, but he later recanted and pleaded not guilty…

name: Alex Batty (found)
summary: Alex Batty of Oldham, England, was 11 when he failed to return from a holiday in Spain with his mother and grandfather in October 2017.

name: Nicola Bulley
summary: Nicola Bulley vanished while walking her dog by the River Wyre in Lancashire, England. Her body was found in the river three weeks later. The case drew massive attention and amateur sleuthing.

name: Holly Wells & Jessica Chapman
summary: Ten-year-olds Holly Wells and Jessica Chapman were murdered by school caretaker Ian Huntley in Soham, Cambridgeshire, in August 2002.

name: Moors Murders Victims
summary: Ian Brady and Myra Hindley killed five children and teenagers in the Manchester area between July 1963 and October 1965, burying four of them on Saddleworth Moor.

name: Fred & Rose West Victims
summary: In February and March 1994, police found the remains of nine young women and girls at 25 Cromwell Street, Gloucester, the home of Fred and Rose West; three more victims were found elsewhere.

name: Peter Tobin Victims
summary: Peter Tobin was convicted of murdering Angelika Kluk, 23, in Glasgow in 2006, and of the 1991 murders of Vicky Hamilton, 15, and Dinah McNicol, 18, whose remains were found in 2007 at a house in Margate, Kent, where he had once…

name: Josef Mengele (fugitive)
summary: Josef Mengele, an SS physician at Auschwitz from 1943 to 1945, fled Germany in 1949 and lived in Argentina, Paraguay and Brazil without ever being arrested.

name: Andrei Chikatilo Victims
summary: Andrei Chikatilo, a former schoolteacher, was found guilty by a court in Rostov-on-Don in October 1992 of murdering 52 women and children between 1978 and 1990 and was sentenced to death.

name: Diane Downs Children
summary: Seven-year-old Cheryl Downs was shot dead and her siblings Christie, 8, and Danny, 3, were badly wounded on a rural road near Springfield, Oregon, on May 19, 1983.

name: David Carrick Victims
summary: Former Metropolitan Police officer David Carrick admitted 49 offences, including 24 counts of rape, against 12 women between 2003 and 2020.

name: John O'Keefe (Karen Read)
summary: Boston police officer John O'Keefe, 46, was found dead in the snow outside a home in Canton, Massachusetts, on January 29, 2022.

name: Riley Strain
summary: University of Missouri senior Riley Strain disappeared on Nashville's Broadway after being kicked out of a bar. His body was found in the Cumberland River two weeks later. His death was ruled accidental drowning.

name: Baby Victoria (daughter of Constance Marten & Mark Gordon)
summary: Newborn Victoria died in early 2023 while her parents, Constance Marten and Mark Gordon, were living in a tent on the South Downs to avoid social services.

name: Lucy Letby Victims
summary: Neonatal nurse Lucy Letby was convicted of murdering seven babies and attempting to murder six others at the Countess of Chester Hospital. She received a whole-life order.

name: Joanna Dennehy Victims
summary: Lukasz Slaboszewski, 31, John Chapman, 56, and Kevin Lee, 48, were stabbed to death in Peterborough, England, in March 2013 and their bodies left in ditches.

name: Natalie McNally
summary: Natalie McNally, 32, who was 15 weeks pregnant, was stabbed to death in her home in Lurgan, Northern Ireland, on December 18, 2022.

name: Brianna Ghey
summary: Sixteen-year-old transgender girl Brianna Ghey was murdered in a park in Warrington by two 15-year-olds. The killers had planned the attack for weeks. Both received life sentences.

name: Jaylen Fleer
summary: San Diego County sheriff's deputy Jaylen Fleer, 27, was arrested in 2020 after Crime Stoppers tips about a man engaging in sex acts with a minor led investigators to him and to four underage victims.

name: Whitey Bulger (death)
summary: Notorious Boston mob boss and longtime FBI informant Whitey Bulger, 89, was beaten to death hours after arriving at USP Hazelton in West Virginia on October 30, 2018.

name: Pamela Smart (case)
summary: Gregg Smart, 24, was shot dead in his Derry, New Hampshire condominium on May 1, 1990 by teenagers recruited by his wife Pamela's student lover, Billy Flynn.

name: Richard Glossip (case)
summary: Motel owner Barry Van Treese was beaten to death at the Best Budget Inn in Oklahoma City in January 1997 by Justin Sneed, who testified that Richard Glossip put him up to it. Glossip was twice convicted and sentenced to death.

name: Natalia Grace Barnett
summary: Michael and Kristine Barnett were charged in 2019 with neglecting their adopted daughter Natalia Grace, a Ukrainian-born girl with a rare form of dwarfism, after allegedly leaving her alone in a Lafayette, Indiana, apartment in…

name: Halyna Hutchins (Rust trial)
summary: Cinematographer Halyna Hutchins, 42, was fatally shot on the set of the film Rust near Santa Fe on October 21, 2021, when a revolver held by actor Alec Baldwin fired a live round.

name: R. Kelly (sentencing)
summary: R&B singer R. Kelly was convicted in New York in September 2021 of racketeering and Mann Act sex trafficking offences and sentenced on June 29, 2022 to 30 years in prison.

name: Tyre Nichols
summary: Tyre Nichols, 29, died on January 10, 2023, three days after being beaten by Memphis police officers following a traffic stop. Former officers Desmond Mills Jr. and Emmitt Martin III pleaded guilty to federal and state charges.
